cells.tense: You've got your hands on the work in front of you, and you're not squeezing it.
cells.ask: Before you get up from where you're sitting, finish one small piece of care all the way — clean up its end, say it's done out loud, and let your shoulders come down.
cells.core:
You pick something up, you tend it while it's yours, and you set it down when it's through — and the setting down doesn't land as a defeat. The people near you get the benefit twice, once while you carry it and once after, when you're not still carrying it out of habit.

Nothing needs fixing here today. When something in front of you wraps up, notice whether the ending feels like an ending or like a loss — and you can finish it either way. The ease, if it's there, is what there is to keep.
cells.sheetLine: You can finish something without turning it into a goodbye.
cells.verb: tending what has been put in your care
cells.place: in a part of life where things have to be let go of, on purpose

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead there's a finish that hasn't happened yet, and you're already standing like it's a cliff edge.
cells.ask: Take one thing you're holding that could end soon and put it out of sight for an hour — closed drawer, next room, phone off — and see that it stays fine without you watching it.
cells.core:
Things still get tended here, and they get tended well — that's not in question. What's different is the grip. You're braced for a version of events that hasn't arrived, and while you brace, the actual thing in front of you is being handled by hands that are half somewhere else. You want it to land well, and the way you're trying to land it is by keeping it in reach the whole time.

The material is steadier than the grip admits. Let one thing finish on its own once, and the ending gets smaller than the one you've been rehearsing — and you can pick the next thing up without the bracing.

cells.tense: You left a door behind you and you're still standing at it.
cells.ask: Pick the smallest unfinished piece of care you've got — a plant, a note, a shelf, a call — give it ten minutes today, and let ten minutes be the whole of it.
cells.core:
In its good form this is work moving through clean: tended while it's yours, set down when it's finished, hands free for the next thing. That shape is still the shape, and right now you're not standing in it. Something ended and you didn't come all the way out with it. You keep half-tending the same thing from a distance, without letting it close, and the standing there costs more than the work would.

Small, real tending — done today, not perfectly — is what gets the current moving again. You don't have to feel ready. You just have to put your hands on one thing.

cells.tense: You're already deciding what stays and what goes, and you're talking about it like weather.
cells.ask: Name one thing you decided to let go of this week, say out loud that you chose it — to the room, or to one person — and sit with it being yours for a beat.
cells.core:
Operating well, this looks like a person who sorts, drops, keeps, and knows the dropping was theirs — the credit travels with the act. You're doing the sorting; the credit isn't travelling. Calls about what stays and what goes have been getting made around you, and when they come up in conversation they arrive as things that happened, not things you did. The care was spent. The one who spent it hasn't said so.

You don't have to keep describing your own decisions as if they landed on you. Take one back in a sentence. That's not an announcement; it's just naming who did it.
